title: Tests: pin the cutter-centre distance of 2D Contour on each route, and prove that the post gate refuses a centreline contour

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
What happens: The radius offset of 2D Contour is proven weakly. Only a plunge-point check of 3.0 +/- 0.25 mm exists. No kept test proves that the post gate catches a centreline path.

Expected: Each route has a test that measures the cutter-centre distance. A test proves that the post gate refuses a centreline contour.

Evidence: Measurement on main d1484f02a (2026-11-15), tool D6. A Trace path with its centre on the edge at full depth was refused: `post blocked - gouge: program cuts below the model in 3136 cell(s), worst 7.00 mm`. No kept test pins this. See #1777 and `operations.rs:2462` `a_closed_chain_routes_the_boundary_path_not_a_centerline`.

Tests to add:
- Picked face and picked closed chain: the min and max distance over all cutting moves is the tool radius, tolerance 0.001 mm.
- Plate with a through hole: the hole ring is one radius inside the hole. The outer ring is one radius outside. Inside on a picked inner ring.
- Control and Wear compensation (`control_comp.rs`): centre moves outside the lead spans stay one radius from the part. `CompSpan.radius` is the tool radius.
- Open boundary route (`contour_open.rs`): an Include boundary edge is cut one radius off on the air side.
- Gate proof: a Trace with the bottom at the part bottom on a box makes `post_setup` return "post blocked - gouge".
- UI: a structural assertion that the Trace / Engrave page says that the tool centre follows the line.

Done means: Each list item has a named test in the default suites.

Related: #1927, #1928
